rules.rule: CV must be in reverse chronological order with no unexplained gaps, using the Europass template, with exact information on studies and practical experience. Documents go to the chosen university, not to DAAD. EPOS also needs proof of at least two years of relevant work experience (employment certificates).

Repeats the rule: Europass template, reverse chronological, no unexplained gaps. The CV is submitted to the university with the signed checklist, the DAAD application form, the motivation letter, employment letters, language certificates and degree certificates.

rules.funder: DAAD EPOS course example: ENREM, TH Köln
rules.rule: Europass format only, maximum 3 pages, dated (current) and signed, reverse chronological with no unexplained gaps. Dates must match every other document submitted. Do not attach certificates to the CV. Individual EPOS courses often add a signature, date or page limit, so read the course checklist.

rules.funder: DAAD EPOS course example: M.Sc. WASTE, Univ. Stuttgart (2026/27)
rules.rule: CV should be in Europass format and carry a date of issue.

rules.funder: DAAD Research Grants (doctoral/research stays; DAAD North America checklist)
rules.rule: Full CV in tabular form, maximum 3 pages. This is where the 'tabular CV' wording comes from. It applies to DAAD research grants, not EPOS. The Africa-region checklist could not be fetched (daad.de scholarship-database pages block automated access), so check the regional checklist.

Students apply directly to each consortium. Each programme sets its own entry requirements and documents, and the Commission prescribes no CV format. Applications typically open between October and January.

rules.funder: Erasmus Mundus example: CLE (European Literary Cultures)
rules.rule: Checklist asks for 'CV (CV Europass)'.
Requires a Europass Curriculum Vitae and links to the template. Many EMJMs follow this pattern, so a Europass CV is the safe default for Erasmus Mundus.

No CV or résumé upload. The online form has an Education history (up to 15 entries) and a Work history (up to 15 entries). The system multiplies weeks by hours per week to check the 2,800-hour requirement. Two reference letters are requested only from applicants who reach the interview stage.

At least 2,800 hours (about 2 years) of work experience gained after the undergraduate degree. Full-time and part-time employment, voluntary work and paid or unpaid internships all count, up to 15 periods. Selectors also weigh the strength of the examples, not only the hours.
No proof of work experience is needed at application. The form asks for employer name, job title and dates. References are verified by the embassy or high commission if the applicant is shortlisted.

Accepted work experience types are full-time, part-time, voluntary work and paid or unpaid internships, all gained after graduating from undergraduate studies. National service (e.g. NYSC) is not named. It falls after graduation, so it is normally entered as an employment period with its real weekly hours. Confirm with Chevening if unsure.

No separate CV is requested. The form has structured fields: all university qualifications, up to 10 publications and prizes, and employment history with an explanation of how it supports the UK programme. Three referees are named (minimum two references). Statements cover development impact, career plans, study plan and a personal statement.

rules.funder: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships for Least Developed Countries and Fragile States (CSC UK)
rules.rule: Open to 17 countries including Nigeria. Ghana and Kenya are NOT eligible. The form fields mirror the master's form: up to 10 publications and prizes, and employment history with its relevance. There is no separate CV.

Many successful applicants hold first-class or distinction degrees, and PhD applicants often have strong publication lists. Common mistakes: brief or weak references ('a five-line reference' is not enough), vague or overly technical writing, generic praise of institutions, and text copied from websites (treated as possible plagiarism).

rules.funder: University of Oxford graduate admissions (Clarendon, Weidenfeld-Hoffmann, other Oxford funding)
rules.rule: Most courses do NOT require a CV. Upload one only if the course page asks for it; unrequested CVs are removed. Where required, keep it to one or two pages ('a page is often enough' at master's level). Suggested sections: Education (with grades), Funding and awards, Publications, Academic or research experience, Other relevant experience, Public engagement.

No separate scholarship application. Applicants to Oxford graduate courses are considered automatically if they apply by the December or January deadline. Selection is on academic merit and potential.

rules.funder: University of Cambridge postgraduate admissions (Gates Cambridge route)
rules.rule: A CV must be uploaded to the Applicant Portal. Cambridge gives no format or length rules. Gates Cambridge applicants nominate an additional referee.

Selection criteria: outstanding intellectual ability, reasons for choice of course, commitment to improving the lives of others, and leadership potential. The CV should give evidence for each, e.g. a service or leadership section with outcomes.

The CV is a form section and cannot be uploaded separately. It allows up to 5 entries in each of: professional/research experience; volunteering, community involvement and leadership; publications and presentations; awards, prizes and scholarships; skills, hobbies and extra-curricular activities. A head-and-shoulders colour photo (jpg) is required, but selectors do not see it until after final shortlisting. The personal statement is limited to 1,000 words.
Exactly one US Letter page, reverse chronological, covering experiences, interests and academic record. No photos or hyperlinks. Use a legible font size. No set format.
Upload a résumé/CV of no more than 2 pages. It should show leadership experiences and accomplishments, professional experience, education and anything not already in the application.

rules.funder: MEXT (Japanese Government) Research Students, embassy-recommended route (UAE embassy example)
rules.rule: Use the prescribed official application form for that year; no free-form CV is requested. Photo: 4.5 x 3.5 cm, upper body, full face, no hat, taken within 6 months, name and nationality on the back. A separate 'Field of Study and Research Plan' sheet is required. Incomplete applications are not considered. The Nigerian embassy publishes its own call, so check it for local details.

Uses set forms: application form, personal statement, study plan, one recommendation on the official form (signed by the recommender and uploaded by the applicant), consent forms, health statement, degrees and transcripts, nationality proof, employment certificate if any. No free-form CV. Published works are optional extras.

No CV. The Personal Profile asks for up to five activities (clubs, family responsibilities, arts, employment, athletics, volunteering, community service) and the applicant's responsibilities in each, in short answers of about 500 to 2,100 characters. UBC may contact the two references to verify activities. Advice: reflect on what you learned rather than listing, and be specific.

Applications go to partner universities or NGOs, not the Foundation. Each partner runs its own admissions and document requirements. The Foundation targets talented, service-oriented young people, including those from underrepresented backgrounds, so an activities/CV list should show service and leadership.
CVs are usually laid out in a clear tabular format, most recent first. 'An application photo is not mandatory, but still widely used.' Europass is suggested for templates.

No photo on UK CVs. Leave out date of birth, gender, marital status and similar; name and contact details are enough. Two pages in reverse chronological order is the standard UK CV. Conventions differ by country, so check country guides.

rules.funder: UK convention (University of Oxford Careers Service)
rules.rule: One or two pages (academic CVs may be longer). Exclude date of birth, age, marital status, children, religion, sex, racial background, disability, home address and basic IT skills. Give nationality only for right-to-work purposes. List referees only on academic CVs. Use 10 to 11 pt or larger, bullets, role on the left and dates on the right, and the CAR pattern (Context, Action, Result).

rules.funder: US convention (Harvard Mignone Center for Career Success)
rules.rule: Résumé sections: Education, Experience, Leadership & Activities, Skills & Interests. Bullets combine action verb, specific accomplishment and quantified result, with no pronouns. Do not include photos, personal demographic details or references.

rules.funder: US academic CV vs résumé (MIT CAPD)
rules.rule: CVs are for academic, research and fellowship applications and give a full scholarly record: 2 to 4 pages early career. Résumés are 1 to 2 pages and focus on relevance. Keep a full master CV and tailor a shorter one for each application.

No fixed length for academic CVs. Publications are among the most important sections: peer-reviewed articles first, reverse chronological, cited as in a journal. Referees should usually include your supervisor and at least one other academic. Always tell referees beforehand.

order: Contact header: full name as on passport/certificates, city and country, email, phone, optional LinkedIn/ORCID. No photo unless the funder or format asks for one (Europass and MEXT forms do; UK/US do not).
Optional 2-3 line profile tied to the target course and goal. No generic 'objective'.
Education, reverse chronological: degree, class or CGPA with scale, thesis title and grade, relevant modules, prizes.
Professional experience, reverse chronological: role, organisation, place, month-year dates, 2-5 achievement bullets.
Research and publications (PhD/academic CVs): peer-reviewed first, then under review, conferences, posters. Use full citations and bold your name.
Leadership, volunteering and community service, with outcomes.
Awards, scholarships and competitions, with selectivity (e.g. '1 of 12 from 400 applicants').
Skills: technical/software, languages (CEFR levels for Europe), certifications.
Referees: named on academic, Europass and Commonwealth-type CVs. Leave them off US résumés.
do: Tailor every version to the funder's criteria: leadership and networking for Chevening; development impact for Commonwealth; intellectual ability, leadership and commitment to others for Gates (cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk, gatescambridge.org).
Write achievement bullets as action verb + task + measurable result (Oxford CAR, Harvard action-verb formula, Cambridge 'Accomplished X as measured by Y by doing Z').
Use numbers: people served, budget, percentage change, ranking, selectivity, time saved.

Keep to 2 pages for master's and job-style CVs. One page for Knight-Hennessy. Schwarzman max 2. DAAD tabular research CV max 3. ENREM-type EPOS courses max 3. Academic CVs may run longer, but put the strongest material on the first two pages (UCL).
Explain every gap of more than about 3 months (EPOS and ENREM require 'no unexplained gaps'), e.g. 'Awaiting NYSC mobilisation; completed online GIS certificate'.
Make dates and titles match your transcripts, employment letters and form entries exactly (ENREM requires this).
Date and sign the CV where the course asks (many EPOS courses).
Use a consistent date format: month and year for UK/US (e.g. 'Sep 2023 - Present'); Europass uses dd/mm/yyyy.
Give CGPA with its scale (e.g. 4.62/5.00, First Class) and, for Europe, explain the grading scale.
Keep a full 'master CV' and cut a tailored version for each application (MIT CAPD).
Tell referees before listing them, and pick people who can write detailed letters; CSC warns that short references score poorly.
Export to PDF, use a readable font of 10-11 pt or larger, and keep consistent bold, italics and spacing.
dont: Don't add a photo, date of birth, marital status, religion, state of origin, gender or number of children to UK/US CVs (Oxford, Cambridge, Manchester, Harvard). Add a photo only when the funder or form requires it (MEXT form; Rhodes WA upload, hidden from selectors until after shortlisting).
Don't open with a long generic 'Career Objective' ('To obtain a challenging position in a reputable organisation...').
Don't send 4-5+ page CVs for master's scholarships, or pad with secondary-school results once you have a degree.
Don't use duty lists ('Responsible for...'), pronouns or passive voice.
Don't list basic IT skills ('Microsoft Word, Internet browsing') or generic hobbies ('reading, travelling, socialising') (Oxford Careers).
Don't upload a CV where none was requested (Oxford removes unrequested CVs) or paste it into form fields without adapting.
Don't copy text from websites or templates. CSC treats copied text as possible plagiarism.
Don't leave typos or inconsistent formatting. Have someone proofread.
Don't overstate: Chevening verifies references and UBC may contact referees to verify activities.
nigeria: NYSC: list it as a real job, e.g. 'Graduate Engineer (NYSC), Ministry of Works, Makurdi | Nov 2022 - Oct 2023', with achievement bullets. Put the CDS project under Leadership/Volunteering with numbers. Chevening counts post-degree work, including voluntary work, so enter NYSC with honest weekly hours; it does not list NYSC by name.
Show the degree class and CGPA with its scale (e.g. 'First Class, CGPA 4.71/5.00'). Add class position only if verifiable.
Use the current university name with the certificate name in brackets if it changed (e.g. 'Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University, Makurdi (formerly University of Agriculture, Makurdi)').

Leave out state of origin, LGA, religion, marital status, date of birth and passport photo for UK/US applications. These are common on Nigerian CVs but marked as irrelevant by UK careers services. Europass optional fields (nationality, DOB) can be left blank.
Translate local acronyms on first use: SIWES (6-month industrial attachment), COREN, NSE, WAEC/NECO, UTME, CDS.
Put SIWES and IT placements under experience for fresh graduates, but don't count pre-graduation work toward Chevening's 2,800 hours.
For undergraduate awards (NLNG, Mastercard partners, UBC), list WAEC/NECO grades and UTME score, school leadership, competitions (olympiads, quiz, JETS), family responsibilities and part-time work.
Use a professional email (firstname.lastname@...) and an international phone format (+234 ...).

JETS (Junior Engineers, Technicians and Scientists) state exhibition, 1st place: low-cost water filter project

sections.note: Competitions show talent beyond grades. The water-filter project ties to the engineering course choice.

entries.title: Shop Assistant, family provisions shop
bullets: Kept daily sales records in a notebook and later Excel; helped cut stock losses by restocking weekly instead of monthly.
Cared for two younger siblings after school while parents worked.

sections.note: UBC explicitly counts family responsibilities and employment as activities. For need-based awards this context explains limited time for clubs.

bullets: Excel (formulas, charts), basic Python (online course, 2025), Scratch
Languages: English (fluent), Igbo (native)
Interests: debate (school team, 2 inter-school trophies), sketching building designs

sections.note: Specific interests with evidence (trophies) rather than 'reading and travelling'. One page in total; don't pad at this stage.

rewrites.strong: Supervised 14 site workers across 3 borehole projects, completing all handovers 2 weeks ahead of schedule.
rewrites.why: Replaces a duty statement with an action verb, scale and a time-based result.

rewrites.weak: Helped with data analysis for the health board.
rewrites.strong: Automated monthly reports for 255 health facilities in Python, cutting preparation time from 5 days to 4 hours.
rewrites.why: 'Helped' hides your role. Naming the tool, the scope and a before-and-after result proves impact.

rewrites.strong: As Welfare Secretary, negotiated a 20% hostel-fee instalment plan adopted for 1,200 students.
rewrites.why: Membership alone shows nothing. A named role and an outcome show leadership.

rewrites.weak: Did my NYSC at the Ministry of Works.
rewrites.strong: Graduate Engineer (NYSC), Ministry of Works: inspected 12 road culverts and produced a repair priority list used in the 2024 budget.
rewrites.why: Frames national service as real professional work with a deliverable someone used.

rewrites.strong: Organised 4 technical seminars averaging 120 attendees and secured N450,000 in sponsorship.
rewrites.why: Numbers show reach and resourcefulness. Sponsorship shows networking (a Chevening criterion).

rewrites.weak: Taught students in a secondary school.
rewrites.strong: Taught physics to 3 SS2 classes (140 students); class pass rate in the WAEC mock rose from 54% to 79%.
rewrites.why: Teaching becomes an outcome: a measurable change in learners' results.

rewrites.strong: Presented water-quality findings to a 9-member state board, securing chlorination at 3 more sites.
rewrites.why: Shows communication through evidence instead of a self-claim, which panels discount.

rewrites.weak: Worked on a research project about malaria.
rewrites.strong: Built a gradient-boosting model predicting district malaria incidence (R^2 = 0.81) from rainfall and clinic data.
rewrites.why: Names the method and reports a result, which signals research ability for academic panels.

rewrites.strong: Recruited 22 volunteers and raised N3.1m to repair 9 hand pumps, restoring water access for about 4,000 people.
rewrites.why: Shows initiative, resource mobilisation and community impact, the core of Commonwealth and Mastercard criteria.

rewrites.weak: Assisted in writing a grant proposal.
rewrites.strong: Drafted the methods section of a USD 180,000 grant proposal, funded in 2025.
rewrites.why: Specifies your contribution, the amount and the successful outcome without overclaiming leadership.
